title: Law Firm Software Build — Dev Strategy, AI & Hiring
tldr: First call with MHM Law Firm, a medium-sized multi-practice firm that has spent ~3 years and significant money building its own legal-practice software with outside dev shops — and feels behind because the prior builds never integrated AI ("everyone's on Xbox, we're on Atari"). The driver: they pay for a stack of disconnected tools (Filevine, Amicus, HotDocs, DocuSign/Adobe, QuickBooks) that don't talk to each other, and estimate an in-house product would pay for itself in ~3 years while also being something they could market and sell to other firms. Top Rock's core reframe: with AI, custom software is now near-commodity — a dev-shop build is the wrong, most expensive path. The recommendation is to hire one strong AI-native engineer in-house (start as a full-time contractor, convert to employee/partner with equity so incentives align), have them start small — nail one feature, then iterate fast rather than rebuild everything. New-grad AI-native talent (e.g. BYU) runs ~$100k/yr; the engineer market is soft right now, so it's a good time to hire. Top Rock won't take the full build (too large for their bandwidth) but will act as thought partner: build clickable prototypes for the firm to play with, and help interview & vet engineering candidates since the partners "don't speak the language." Top Rock to send recap notes + a high-level proposal; MHM to think about the shift from outsourcing to an in-house hire and tap their network for the right engineer.

actionItems.action: Send MHM the recap / feedback notes from this meeting.
Put together a high-level proposal / recommendation (in-house hire + Top Rock support).
Offer to build clickable prototypes of key concepts for MHM to play with.
Be available to interview & technically vet engineering candidates when MHM has them.
Reflect on the shift from outsourcing to an in-house hire.
Tap the firm's network for referrals to a strong AI-native engineer.
Gather what's needed (access / screenshots) to assess how much of the 3-year build is usable.
